method: The product space of Hidalgo, Klinger, Barabási and Hausmann (2007) from the Growth Lab's HS92 trade data: Balassa RCA on three-year averages, proximity on economies exporting at least US$1 billion, density of each product in each economy's basket. The discovery gap: for every product an economy did not export competitively at the start of a five-year window (RCA below 0.5, mining, fuel, precious metals, stamps, art and scrap left out), the chance it was exported competitively (RCA of 1 or more) at the end, from a logistic regression across all economy-products on density (a cubic), the starting RCA and log income per head; expected entries are the sum of the chances, and the gap is actual minus expected in binomial standard deviations.
source: Growth Lab International Trade Data (HS92), doi:10.7910/DVN/T4CHWJ, via data/silver/hs4_exports.parquet; income from the snapshot (NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.KD).
